crop.notes: Whole feature including headline, illustrations and fight record.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic profiled Allen, 54, at his Champion's Rest saloon. He recalled his fights with Gallagher, McCool, Mace and Goss, his 23 battles from 1860 to 1879 and his career record.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic, St. Louis, Sunday Morning, March 31, 1895, page 40.

facts.fact: The Republic said Allen fought 23 battles between 1860 and 1879 and supplied a summary record of his English and American fights
Allen beat Bill Davis in 43 rounds in his first American fight
Allen lost to Charley Gallagher in two rounds after slipping on a snow-filled hole in the ring and being hit on the neck (the text gives Feb. 22; the record table gives Feb. 23)
Allen and Mike McCool fought a draw at Foster's Island when the McCool party broke into the ring after the ninth or tenth round

Allen beat Charley Gallagher in 11 rounds (21 minutes) at Chouteau Island; he was shot through the back of the right hand mid-fight and the bullet was pushed out so the fight could resume; he said he knew who fired and it was meant for him
Allen lost the championship of the world to Jem Mace in ten rounds (50 minutes) at New Orleans, breaking his arm
A McCool match for $2,500 a side fell through when McCool forfeited $1,000; Allen was then in New York sparring in exhibitions with Mace
Allen beat Jim Gallagher in 14 rounds (21 minutes) on a sandbar at the foot of Chouteau Avenue, staking $1,000 to $500
places: Foot of Chouteau Avenue, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen beat Mike McCool in seven rounds for $2,000 a side and the championship; the boat money on his second McCool fight was $12,000, half to Allen
Allen beat Ben Hogan in three rounds; Hogan's friends rushed the ring and pointed pistols at him

Allen fought Joe Goss in Kentucky; referee Eph Holland gave the fight to Goss on an alleged foul and Holland kept Fred Watkins's $1,000 stake; Allen left by way of Canada for England and Goss served a year and a half in prison
Allen returned to England and beat Tompkin Gilbert in five rounds
Allen beat Professor Charles Davis in five rounds at Cambridge Hall, West London, winning the championship of England and a silver cup inscribed May 22, 1878
Allen beat Jim Stewart in 16 rounds in England, his last fight before coming home
Allen lived above his Champion's Rest saloon on Market Street near Seventh, with the English championship cup in a glass case behind the bar
places: Market Street near Seventh, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen said Corbett was the best man of them all and would find Fitzsimmons an easy job
facts.quote: I'm of the notion that the best man of 'em all now is Corbett.

notes: The record table gives nine rounds for the McCool draw where the prose says ten, and Feb. 23 against the prose's Feb. 22 for the first Gallagher fight; age given as 54 and later 56. Allen's fight summary table is a good source for a fight record.
